clue.text: Bounder in song by Jacopo Sannazaro

indicators.note: in places the word for the bounder inside the word for the song

parts.note: an aria is a song for a solo voice in opera
a bounder is a cad, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A cad turns up in a song written by the Neapolitan poet Sannazaro.
explanation.walkthrough: Sannazaro's Arcadia (1504) is a pastoral romance in prose and verse, so the definition is the work 'by' him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance poet Sannazaro wrote the pastoral romance of that name, a founding text of the genre.

clue.text: Leaser got arrangement for intimate friends

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters of leaser and got sets them in a new order

explanation.surface: A landlord made a deal for close friends.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self, hence a trusted bosom companion.

clue.text: He provides the stuff of knowledge

definitions.text: He provides the stuff of knowledge

parts.words: He provides the stuff of knowledge
parts.note: stuff is a verb: this is someone who stuffs pupils' heads with facts before an exam

explanation.definitionFit: A crammer is a tutor or school that drills students intensively for examinations.

clue.text: Jacobean sleuth, you might say

parts.note: Jacobean suggests the reign of James I, but means belonging to the crime novelist P. D. James

explanation.definitionFit: Commander Adam Dalgliesh is the poet-detective of P. D. James's novels.

clue.text: An impersonal French subject isa most prolific writer

parts.note: on is the French impersonal pronoun meaning one

explanation.surface: A French grammar point is the most productive author of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isa' is the paper's run-together 'is a', a link. The writer is Anonymous, credited with more works than anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon., short for anonymous, is credited with countless poems and ballads of unknown authorship.

clue.text: Chronicler of pilgrims' progress

parts.note: hints at Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, but means the poet who recorded a pilgrimage to Canterbury, telling the travellers' tales

explanation.definitionFit: The Canterbury Tales follow a band of pilgrims on their way to the shrine of Becket.

clue.text: Yet them nor peer nor prince can buy, / Till —, themselves do cry (Campion)

definitions.text: Yet them nor peer nor prince can buy, / Till —, themselves do cry (Campion)

parts.words: Yet them nor peer nor prince can buy, / Till —, themselves do cry (Campion)
parts.note: the solver completes Thomas Campion's song There is a garden in her face, whose lips are likened to fruit offered by a street seller's cry

explanation.definitionFit: The refrain of Campion's song echoes the London street cry selling ripe cherries.

clue.text: Musketeer in Macedonia

explanation.definitionFit: One of Dumas's three swordsmen bears the name, as does the monastic mountain in Greek Macedonia.

clue.text: Property, possibly latchet

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of latchet may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A shoe fastening might count as a possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is an item of movable personal property.

clue.text: Dickens character who kept his Grip

definitions.text: Dickens character who kept his Grip

parts.words: Dickens character who kept his Grip
parts.note: Grip seems to mean self-control, but is the talking raven owned by the simple-minded hero of one Dickens novel

explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby, title hero of Dickens's 1841 novel, carries his pet raven Grip everywhere.

clue.text: Track dog

explanation.definitionFit: Track is a path or a set of tracks left behind; to dog someone is to follow them closely.

clue.text: Eavesdropped Ustinov piece

explanation.definitionFit: Eavesdropped means listened in secretly; Peter Ustinov wrote a stage play of that title (1981).

clue.text: Florentine heroine is no neophyte in capital

indicators.note: in puts the letters for no and neophyte inside the capital

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name of the capital city of Italy
O is nought, a zero or nothing
L stands for learner, a beginner

explanation.surface: A Florentine heroine is anything but a novice in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroine is George Eliot's novel of Renaissance Florence; L is the learner plate British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's 1863 novel is named for its heroine, a woman of fifteenth-century Florence.

clue.text: Rites get involved for working girl

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so the letters of rites and get are mixed up

explanation.surface: Ceremonies become complicated for a girl with a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A grisette was a young French working-class woman, often a shop or garment worker.

clue.text: Some of his characters seem to have found him elusive

definitions.text: Some of his characters seem to have found him elusive

parts.words: Some of his characters seem to have found him elusive
parts.note: alludes to the play Six Characters in Search of an Author, whose figures hunt for their writer

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian dramatist wrote the play in which six characters go looking for an author.

clue.text: Russian novelist written up in Henrik Rogersson's work

indicators.note: written up in a down entry means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
in shows the letters sit within the words Henrik Rogersson's

explanation.surface: A Russian writer is reviewed in a Scandinavian author's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxim Gorky (also spelt Gorki) was the Russian writer of Mother and The Lower Depths.

clue.text: "Guerrilar" wrongly spells a Holmes guerrilla

indicators.note: wrongly says the misspelt word is put right by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A misspelling of guerrilla gives a word for one of Sherlock Holmes's street helpers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Baker Street Irregulars were the street urchins Holmes used as informal agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular soldier, and Holmes's band of street boys were so named.

clue.text: Jungle baby from colourless Staffs town

parts.note: grey means drab or colourless
Stoke-on-Trent is a town in Staffordshire, an English county abbreviated Staffs

explanation.surface: A child of the wild comes from a dreary Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarzan was born John Clayton, heir to Lord Greystoke, and raised by apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan, raised by apes in the jungle as an infant, was the heir of the Earl of that title.

clue.text: Live, to a point, with church support in abode

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere
N, north, is a point of the compass
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Settle somewhere up to a point, with backing from the church, in a dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a' adds the point to RESIDE; 'support' and 'in' merely link the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a home or dwelling place.

clue.text: "He'd make a lovely corpse" (— —)

parts.note: the solver must supply the speaker of this line, the gin-loving nurse and layer-out in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit

explanation.definitionFit: The monthly nurse in Martin Chuzzlewit says this of a patient, in keeping with her trade of laying out the dead.

clue.text: Deserter under twenty, in coarse cloth

parts.note: a rat is someone who deserts a cause, as rats leave a sinking ship
a teen is aged under twenty

explanation.surface: A young runaway is dressed in rough fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratteen is a thick twilled woollen fabric.

clue.text: Former post offices used for displays

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
PO is the abbreviation for post office, so two are POs

explanation.surface: Disused post office buildings are turned into exhibition halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Expos are exhibitions or shows, where goods are put on view.

clue.text: Superb, that is, as a bishop

parts.note: proud can mean splendid or superb

explanation.surface: Being haughty is fitting for a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop Proudie is the henpecked prelate of Trollope's Barchester novels.
explanation.definitionFit: In Trollope's Barchester novels the Bishop of Barchester bears this name.

clue.text: Writers' blocks?

parts.note: plays on writer's block, the inability to write, but means pads of paper that writers jot on

explanation.definitionFit: Pads are blocks of paper sheets used for jotting down memos.

clue.text: This ancestor of David was not ruthless

definitions.text: This ancestor of David was not ruthless

parts.words: This ancestor of David was not ruthless
parts.note: ruthless means without Ruth: this biblical woman kept her daughter-in-law Ruth, the great-grandmother of King David, at her side

explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth the widow from Bethlehem is accompanied home by Ruth, from whom David descends.

clue.text: Location of E. Bowen's

parts.note: the possessive points to Elizabeth Bowen's novel The House in ..., naming the city where her house stands

explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Bowen's 1935 novel is The House in that French capital.

clue.text: Demons exorcised by Thackeray's Henry

indicators.note: exorcised suggests the demons are driven out and disturbed, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Thackeray's hero casts out evil spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The History of Henry Esmond is Thackeray's historical novel named for its hero.

clue.text: How to relax with Johnsonian essays?

definitions.text: How to relax with Johnsonian essays?

parts.words: How to relax with Johnsonian essays?
parts.note: Samuel Johnson wrote a series of essays called The ..., so relaxing in their company is to do nothing

explanation.definitionFit: To do nothing and loaf about is to be at leisure, and Johnson's essays bore a related title.

clue.text: Reversed Shaw piece

explanation.definitionFit: A ruling that is reversed has been overturned by higher authority; Overruled is also a one-act comedy by Bernard Shaw.

clue.text: Ancient, obsolete lazy days entirely natural to start with

indicators.note: to start with tells us to take the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: Old times were idle days, wholly natural and long gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an old-fashioned word for long past, as in olden days.

clue.text: His dramatic output was absurd

parts.note: reads as an insult to a playwright, but alludes to the Theatre of the Absurd, of which this Romanian-French writer was a leading figure

explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Bald Soprano and Rhinoceros is a central name in the Theatre of the Absurd.

clue.text: Interpreter (divorcee for example) takes summer in Paris

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse, as a divorcee is
été is French for summer

explanation.surface: An interpreter, a divorced woman, spends the summer in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: An exegete explains and expounds texts, especially scripture.
